h1:
Prachinburi Travel Tips
When to Go + What It Costs
intro: Prachinburi sits only about 135 km from Bangkok, roughly an hour and a half to two hours by car. It's a year-round province, but each season has its own feel. The cool season is comfortable for the Khao Yai approach on this side, the rainy season brings strong water that's perfect for rafting the Hin Phoeng rapids, and June to July is the sweet santol season that locals are proud of. This article breaks down when to go, what to pack, and how much it costs.

blocks.html: To get the most out of Prachinburi, the first thing to decide is "what do you want to do," because the province's main activities are clearly tied to the seasons. Hin Phoeng rafting only runs in the rainy season, santol ripens for just a short window mid-year, and the Khao Yai approach on the Prachinburi side is doable all year but is coolest and greenest in winter. Match your timing to the activity you want and the trip comes together far better than just going on whatever long weekend lands.

blocks.text: Best time to visit Prachinburi — by activity

blocks.html: Prachinburi doesn't have one single "best time," because each activity peaks at a different point. The rough table below helps you see which month suits what you're after.

items: November–February (cool season) — the best window for the Khao Yai approach on the Prachinburi side. Cool air, morning mist, easy waterfall hikes. It's the province's high season, so weekends get busy and rooms fill fast.

June–July — Prachinburi's sweet santol season. Stop by roadside fruit markets and santol orchards. Rain starts around now but isn't heavy yet, so in-town sights and the herbal route are still comfortable.

July–October (rainy season) — Hin Phoeng rafting season. The water in the Sai Yai river is high and strong, the rapids are fun, the waterfalls are full, and the forest is deep green — just be ready for rain and wet roads.

March–May (hot season) — the quietest stretch. Hot weather and low water at some falls, but the upside is fewer people and cheaper rooms. Good for café-hoppers, herbal-route fans, and anyone who dislikes crowds.

blocks.title: Quick summary
blocks.html: Want cool air and Khao Yai → cool season · Want rafting → July onward · Want santol → June–July · Want to skip the crowds and save money → hot season

blocks.text: Cool season — Khao Yai's Prachinburi side, the province's peak

blocks.html: Khao Yai National Park spans four provinces, and the Prachinburi side is the southern way up. You enter through the Nern Hom checkpoint via Mueang district. This route sees fewer people than the Pak Chong side and feels quieter. From November to February the mornings are cool — great for hiking, waterfalls, and wildlife spotting.

items: Haew Narok Waterfall — the big multi-tier falls that are the highlight on this side. In the cool season the water looks great and the walk is easier than the slippery trails of the rainy months.
Hiking trails and viewpoints — there are several routes inside the park. Cool-season skies are clear, so you can see far.
Pack a light jacket — mornings and nights up on the mountain are noticeably cooler than in town.

blocks.title: Park entry fee
blocks.html: Khao Yai charges Thai adults around 40 THB, children 20 THB, plus about 30 THB per car. Check the latest rate at the checkpoint, since it can change.

blocks.text: Rainy season — Hin Phoeng rafting, a highlight open only part of the year

blocks.html: Hin Phoeng rafting sits inside Khao Yai National Park, in Na Di district, Prachinburi. It only runs in the rainy season, roughly July to October, because it depends on the Sai Yai river being high and strong enough. In the dry season the water is too low to raft. Every year there's a Hin Phoeng rafting festival around August that officially opens the season.

items: Difficulty — the rapids come in several grades, from gentle up to class 3–5 when the water is strong. It's fun, but listen to your guide and keep your life vest on the whole time.
Book ahead — use the raft and guide services run by operators around Sai Yai/Na Di, and reserve your slot in advance, especially on long weekends.
What to bring — strapped sandals or shoes you don't mind getting wet, a change of clothes for after, and a waterproof pouch for your phone.
Allow extra travel time — the rafting put-in is deep into Na Di, far from Prachinburi town, so budget time for the drive and rainy-season road conditions.

blocks.title: Rough pricing
blocks.html: Rafting is usually charged per raft/per person, anywhere from a few hundred to around a thousand-plus THB depending on the distance and operator. A 2-day, 1-night package that includes lodging and rafting commonly runs around 5,500 THB per person. Check the price with each operator before booking.

Prachinburi is known for santol, especially the Pui Fai and E-La varieties with their thick, soft, sweet flesh. The fruit ripens mid-year, around June to July, when orchards and roadside markets stock fresh santol, durian, mangosteen, and bamboo shoots all at once. It's a great moment for anyone who loves seasonal fruit.

items.name: Nong Cha-om Market
items.blurb: Prachinburi's local fruit market. Mid-year it has fresh santol and seasonal fruit, along with processed goods, all at local prices.

items.name: Roadside orchards
items.blurb: From June to July, some orchards open for you to stop and buy santol straight from the source, and a few let you taste before you buy.

blocks.html: If you want to dig into santol specifically — the varieties, prices, and where to buy — we have a separate article linked below to read next.

blocks.text: Day trip from Bangkok — is it doable, and which route?

blocks.html: Prachinburi makes an easy day trip from Bangkok. It's about 135 km, driving via the motorway / Suwannason Road (Highway 33), roughly 1.5–2 hours. Leave early and you can cover the in-town sights and the herbal route in a single day. But if you also want to head up Khao Yai or go rafting, staying one night keeps things from feeling rushed.

blocks.label: Herbal + history day trip
blocks.title: In-town sights and Si Mahosot, there and back in one day

items.note: Take Highway 33 toward Prachinburi; grab coffee along the way.
See the yellow European-style Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building, take photos, and pick up herbal products.
Stroll the garden to learn about medicinal plants, then stop at a café / health-food spot on site.
Try boat noodles or local Prachinburi dishes.

items.activity: Si Maha Pho tree, Si Mahosot district
items.note: An ancient bodhi tree and the old city of Si Mahosot, traces of Dvaravati civilization.
An ancient pond and a pair of Buddha footprints nearby; a short walk to see them.
Get home before dark and avoid the inbound traffic.

blocks.label: Nature day trip
blocks.title: Khao Yai, Prachinburi side, there and back (best in cool season)

items.note: The earlier the better — cooler air and fewer people.

items.activity: Up Khao Yai via the Nern Hom checkpoint
items.note: The Prachinburi-side way up, less crowded than the Pak Chong side.
Walk the multi-tier falls, the highlight on this side.
Pack your own meal or use the park's food service points.
Pick a route that fits your time and ask the rangers which trails are open.

items.activity: Head down and back to Bangkok
items.note: Come down before dark since the mountain road is winding.

blocks.title: No private car
blocks.html: There are Bangkok–Prachinburi buses from Mo Chit, with fares in the low hundreds of THB and a roughly 3.5-hour ride. But nature spots like Khao Yai and the rafting are hard to reach onward, so renting a car or going with a tour/package that includes transfers is the way to go.

blocks.text: Budget — how much does a Prachinburi trip cost?

blocks.html: Prachinburi can be done on the cheap. If you drive yourself and stick to in-town sights and the herbal route, the per-person budget stays low. Nature outings and rafting add activity costs. The figures below are per-person estimates so you can plan.

items.name: Budget day trip (there and back in a day)
items.blurb: Drive yourself, do the herbal-history route in town. Most stops are free or cheap, so you mainly pay for fuel, food, and souvenirs.
items.meta: Per person · excludes the car; splitting it among several people makes it even cheaper

items.name: Khao Yai day trip, Prachinburi side
items.blurb: Add park entry, fuel for the climb, and meals. Best in the cool season.

items.name: One night in town
items.blurb: A mid-range room in Prachinburi town runs from the low hundreds to a thousand-plus THB a night, with food and two days of sightseeing.

items.name: Hin Phoeng rafting package, 2 days 1 night
items.blurb: A package with lodging, rafting, meals, and transport, commonly around 5,500 THB per person. Best in the rainy season.

blocks.title: Save more
blocks.html: Going with a group and splitting the car/room cuts costs a lot, and many of Prachinburi's highlights — the Abhaibhubejhr building, the herb garden, the Si Mahosot bodhi tree — are free or charge very little.

blocks.text: Before you go — a short checklist

items: Match the season to the activity — especially rafting (rainy season) and santol (mid-year); don't show up in the wrong window and miss out.
Clothes for the season — pack a light jacket for the cool-season mountain, and rain gear plus shoes you don't mind getting wet for the rainy season.
Book ahead on long weekends — rooms and rafting slots fill fast in high season and on weekends.
Allow travel time within the province — nature spots are far from town and rainy-season roads can be slow.
Carry cash — fruit markets, orchards, and many local shops are easier to pay with cash.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Prachinburi?
faq.a: It depends on what you want to do. The cool season (November–February) is best for the Khao Yai approach on the Prachinburi side because of the cool air. The rainy season (July–October) is Hin Phoeng rafting season. And June–July is sweet santol season. Match your timing to the activity you want.

faq.q: What months is Hin Phoeng rafting open?
faq.a: Hin Phoeng rafting, inside Khao Yai National Park in Na Di district, runs only in the rainy season, roughly July to October, because it needs the Sai Yai river to be high and strong enough. In the dry season the water is too low to raft. Every year a rafting festival around August opens the season.

faq.q: Can you do Prachinburi as a day trip from Bangkok?
faq.a: Yes. It's about 135 km, a 1.5–2 hour drive. Leave early and you can cover the herbal and history sights in town in a single day. But if you also plan to head up Khao Yai or go rafting, staying one night keeps it from feeling rushed.

faq.q: How much does a Prachinburi trip cost?
faq.a: A budget in-town day trip runs around 500–900 THB per person, a Khao Yai day trip around 700–1,200 THB, one night around 1,500–2,500 THB, and a commonly seen 2-day, 1-night rafting package around 5,500 THB per person.

faq.q: What month is Prachinburi santol in season?
faq.a: Prachinburi santol ripens mid-year, around June to July, especially the Pui Fai and E-La varieties. You can buy it at Nong Cha-om Market and roadside orchards. Durian and mangosteen come out in the same window too.
